name: Qdrant (Qdrant Solutions GmbH)
origin_detail: Rust vector search engine whose GitHub repo dates from May 2020; company founded out of Berlin in 2021 by Andre Zayarni (CEO) and Andrey Vasnetsov (CTO); managed cloud launched early 2023
openness_notes: Initial 3, current 3. The whole engine has been Apache-2.0 since the LICENSE file was created on 2021-04-07; the only later LICENSE commit (2026-08-31) added Qdrant Solutions GmbH as copyright holder and did not change the licence. No enterprise edition of the engine was found: paid tiers differ by managed-service and operations features (HA, backups, SLAs, enterprise SSO, private VPC links), and the managed-cloud service around Managed/Hybrid/Private Cloud is sold separately from the open engine (its source status was not checked). So substantially the whole product is OSI-licensed and money comes from hosting (level 3). Unlike MongoDB, Elastic, Redis and HashiCorp (2018-2024), Qdrant has not relicensed.

license_history.note: LICENSE file created 2021-04-07; unchanged through Nov 2026 except the copyright-holder line added 2026-08-31

risk_events: No licence change through Nov 2026: the Apache-2.0 engine can be hosted by anyone, including hyperscalers, so the managed cloud must compete on operations rather than exclusivity
robustness: Permissively licensed Rust engine with broad adoption (over 250 million package downloads and 29,000+ GitHub stars by Mar 2026; 35,680 stars Nov 2026), so the code would outlive the company, but development and governance are controlled by one VC-backed firm with no foundation.
physical_science_relevance: General retrieval infrastructure for RAG and similarity search over embeddings (documents, images, and in principle molecular or materials embeddings); no science-specific deployments were confirmed on fetched pages beyond customers such as Roche.
openness_effect_assessment: Staying fully Apache-2.0 has not stopped Qdrant from raising successively larger rounds ($7.5M seed 2023, $28M Series A 2024, $50M Series B 2026) or winning enterprise customers (Canva, HubSpot, Roche, Bosch), with the open engine acting as the funnel (5M+ downloads at the Series A, 250M+ by the Series B) for paid managed, hybrid and private cloud. There is no sign yet of the defensive relicensing that earlier database vendors adopted once cloud providers competed with them.
key_takeaway: Qdrant is a clean AI-era example of permissive open source as a startup strategy: a Berlin vector database that has stayed Apache-2.0 since 2021, makes money from hosted and private-cloud deployments, and had raised about $88M by March 2026 without disclosing a valuation. Whether it keeps the licence once hyperscalers offer it as a service, the trigger for the 2018-2024 relicensing wave, is the open question.
